summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change definitions in the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 and create express discrimination exemptions for services, activities and spaces reserved exclusively for women.
It would define sex in biological, binary terms, reintroduce definitions of man and woman, and describe gender identity as a person's self-determined classification.
Sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex status would remain protected attributes, alongside the proposed exceptions for services, spaces and activities reserved for women.
changes: The sexual orientation definition would use opposite-sex language in place of different-sex wording.
The intersex status definition would be replaced with references to differences in sexual development.
The gender identity discrimination comparator would refer to someone who is not of that identity.
References to designated sex at birth would be removed from the gender identity definition.
summary.affected: People covered by sex discrimination protections and operators of women's services, activities and facilities are affected.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Willcox
speeches.brief: Supported the Sex Discrimination Amendment (Sex-based Rights) Bill 2026, arguing that restoring biological definitions of man and woman and replacing 'different sex' with 'opposite sex' would protect women-only spaces, services, sports and privacy. Speakers said the bill would not attack transgender Australians and described current legal protections as inadequate; the debate was adjourned.
